To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the semantic and spatio-temporal context of a query can be effectively captured and used to support the presentation of results; (b) this approach can support both directed and exploratory search strategies; and (c) the presentation of results can be made more effective by using a combination of visual, textual, and spatial cues.

the semantic and spatio-temporal correlations amongst the retrieved data can be exploited to provide an alternative presentation paradigm that is more conducive to the assimilation and understanding of the information.
the presentation of results can be enhanced by using the semantic correlations amongst retrieved results and by utilizing the spatio-temporal aspects of the results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
rethinking the presentation of results of a search.
developing new paradigms for the presentation of search results.
the development of a new paradigm for the presentation and display of results from Web searches that is more conducive to assimilation of information and supports a broader range of user needs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work represents a significant step towards a more effective, efficient, and intuitive presentation of results from information retrieval systems.
the proposed system provides a new way of viewing search results that is both intuitive and useful.
the proposed system has the potential to provide a new paradigm for information retrieval that is both intuitive as well as efficient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach to information access and presentation that is based on a combination of semantic, spatial, temporal, and visual information.

we are developing a system which would be capable of supporting the entire spectrum of search behaviors, ranging from direct, specific, and focused queries to exploratory, open ended, and more general queries, in a manner that would be both intuitive and easy to use.
we have developed a novel approach to present results from Web search.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presentation of the results of a search is as important as the search itself.

a more intelligent presentation of results, which is sensitive to the semantics and context of the query, can be of immense help to the user in assimilating and making use of the retrieved information.
the presentation of results of a query should be done in a manner that retains and displays context and supports both direct search behavior and exploratory search strategies.
